title: RTX GPU Unlock 2026: What It Means for Local LLMs
description: RTX GPU unlock doubles some tensor math on RTX 20, 30 and 40 cards, yet token generation stays flat. Which local LLM work speeds up, and when a Mac still wins.

attribution.citation: Json House, "RTX GPU Unlock 2026: What It Means for Local LLMs", jsonhouse.com (2026-10-30)

key_facts.fact: gpu-unlock removes a half-rate cap on FP16, BF16, and TF32 tensor math with FP32 accumulation on RTX 20, 30, and 40 cards; RTX 30 is listed as stable and RTX 20 and 40 as experimental
The project reports +25–55% for LLM prompt processing on FP16, BF16, AWQ, or GPTQ models, and no change for LLM decode and token generation
The project reports 0–15% for quantized GGUF models in llama.cpp and Ollama, mostly at long context
The README lists the RTX 3070 at 40 to 72 TFLOPS in BF16 dense matrix multiplication; the unlock does not change its 8GB of memory
The main gpu-unlock project is Linux only and its author does not plan to maintain Windows; a separate community port is experimental
Mac Studio M5 Max with the 40-core GPU offers 614 GB/s and up to 128GB; DGX Spark offers 273 GB/s and up to 128GB, a 2.25x bandwidth difference by Json House arithmetic
Press reports put the 128GB DGX Spark at $6,950 and a new 64GB model at $4,999 in October 2026
Used RTX 3090 price sources in September and October 2026 ranged from about $1,199 to about $1,450, against a $1,499 launch price

faq_summary.q: Does gpu-unlock make local LLMs generate tokens faster?
faq_summary.a: No. The project lists token generation as no change because it is limited by memory bandwidth. Prompt processing improves by a reported +25–55% on FP16, BF16, AWQ, or GPTQ models.

faq_summary.q: Does gpu-unlock speed up Ollama or llama.cpp?
faq_summary.a: Barely. The project reports 0–15% for quantized GGUF models, mostly at long context.
Not in the main project, which is Linux only. A separate community port has success reports on specific cards and systems, but it is experimental.

faq_summary.q: Is a Mac better than DGX Spark for local LLMs?
faq_summary.a: For one person running large models, published numbers favor the Mac Studio M5 Max: 614 GB/s against 273 GB/s at 128GB, at what appears to be a lower price. DGX Spark's strongest reasons to buy are CUDA and batched serving.
